messages.subject: multiple groups analysis in Lavaan
parts:
Hi all,
I want to fit multiple group model in Lavaan for the Cohort sequential design. I could not find an option, which would enable to fit different models to individual groups, which contain slightly different variables, i.e. for the first group I have variables for time t1, t2, t3, t4, for the second cohort data from t2,t3,t4,t5. I need to fit a 2-group model with appropriate across-group equality constraints. Is there any possibility, how to deal with this issue In Lavaan (I know it can be done in Amos but it is not an option for me)?
THanks,
Martin

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: multiple groups analysis in Lavaan
parts:
On 12/02/2014 11:03 AM, marti...@gmail.com wrote:
> Hi all,
> I want to fit multiple group model in Lavaan for the Cohort sequential
> design. I could not find an option, which would enable to fit different
> models to individual groups, which contain slightly different variables

It can be done, although this 'feature' of lavaan has not been tested
very well (is probably not even documented). As an example:

library(lavaan)

HS.model <- '
group 1:
visual =~ x1 + a*x2 + b*x3
textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6

group 2:
visual =~ x1 + a*x2 + b*x3
speed =~ x7 + x8 + x9
'

fit <- cfa(HS.model, data=HolzingerSwineford1939, group="school")

Yves.

That's great, thank you very much. I used the feature to the example of cohort sequential design described in Preachers' at al. book. The result was as expected (i.e. the value of chi-square statistics and paarameter estimates), except the number of df. I was expecting 22 df: 28 distinct sample moments (10 variances and covariances and 4 means per group) - 6 free parameters to be estimated (I tried also Amos with this result), but Lavaan showed me 34 df. Do you have any idea, what can be wrong?

require(lavaan)

coh1_lower<-'
 7.1309
 3.7271 7.3845
 4.6564 5.7800 10.0728
 4.4479 5.0547 6.2515 9.8391 '

coh2_lower<-'
  7.9986
 6.3837 11.6301
 5.2663 7.0658 10.7537
 5.6107 7.2714 7.4870 13.0550 '

datac1.cov <- 
    getCov(coh1_lower, names = c("x1", "x2", "x3", "x4"))

datac2.cov <- 
    getCov(coh2_lower, names = c("x2", "x3", "x4", "x5"))

model8 <- ' 
     group 1:
     i1 =~ 1*x1 + 1*x2 + 1*x3 + 1*x4
     s1 =~ 0*x1 + 2*x2 + 3*x3 + 4*x4
     
     x1~~residual*x1
     x2~~residual*x2
     x3~~residual*x3
     x4~~residual*x4
     
     i1~meani*1
     i1~~vari*i1
     s1~means*1
     s1~~vars*s1
     i1~~cov*s1

     group 2:       
     i2 =~ 1*x2 + 1*x3 + 1*x4 + 1*x5
     s2 =~ 2*x2 + 3*x3 + 4*x4 + 5*x5
           
           
     x2~~residual*x2
     x3~~residual*x3
     x4~~residual*x4
     x5~~residual*x5
           
     i2~meani*1
     i2~~vari*i2
     s2~means*1
     s2~~vars*s2
     i2~~cov*s2'          
                  
fit <- growth(model8, sample.cov=list(datac1.cov, datac2.cov), sample.nobs=c(426, 467), 
              sample.mean=list(c(37.9437, 37.2089, 36.9155, 36.4852), c(37.2762, 37.1334, 36.6296, 36.2976)),group.label=c("kohorta1","kohorta2"))

summary(fit, fit.measures=TRUE)

messages.subject: Re: multiple groups analysis in Lavaan
parts:
On 12/03/2014 04:37 PM, marti...@gmail.com wrote:
> That's great, thank you very much. I used the feature to the example of
> cohort sequential design described in Preachers' at al. book. The result
> was as expected (i.e. the value of chi-square statistics and paarameter
> estimates), except the number of df. I was expecting 22 df: 28 distinct
> sample moments (10 variances and covariances and 4 means per group) - 6
> free parameters to be estimated (I tried also Amos with this result),
> but Lavaan showed me 34 df. Do you have any idea, what can be wrong?

This is a bug. The way the sample statistics are counted in lavaan is
currently (0.5-17) wrong, *if* you have a different set of variables per
group. (But this is an unsupported feature; will try to fix this soon).

Yves.
